public import FormalConjecturesUtil


/-!
# Mean value problem

*Reference:*
- [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mean_value_problem)
- [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
by Steve Smale

Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ K* |p'(z)|$ for $K=1$.


The conjecture has been proven for:
* `K = 4`
  [The fundamental theorem of algebra and complexity theory](https://www.ams.org/journals/bull/1981-04-01/S0273-0979-1981-14858-8/)
  by *Steve Smale*
* `K = (d-1)/d` at a point $z$ if the normalised polynomial $p(X + z) - p(z)$ has only real
  roots, or if all its nonzero roots have the same norm.
  [Critical points and values of complex polynomials](https://doi.org/10.1016/0885-064X(89)90019-8)
  by *David Tischler*
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace MeanValueProblem

/--
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there is a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ |p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following weaker version of the mean value problem has been proven.
Given a complex polynomial $p$ of degree $d ≥ 2$ and a complex number $z$
there a critical point $c$ of $p$, such that $|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| ≤ 4|p'(z)|$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_leq_4 (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.degree) (z : ℂ) (K : ℝ):
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ 4 *‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$ has been shown by
Tischler. Let $z$ be a complex number such that the normalised polynomial $p(X + z) - p(z)$ has
only real roots, i.e. every $x$ with $p(x) = p(z)$ satisfies
$\operatorname{Im} x = \operatorname{Im} z$. Then there is a critical point $c$ of $p$ such that
$|p(z)-p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_real_roots (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (z : ℂ)
    (h : ∀ x : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → x.im = z.im) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

/--
The following tighter bound depending on the degree $d$ of the polynomial $p$ has been shown by
Tischler. Let $z$ be a complex number such that all nonzero roots of the normalised polynomial
$p(X + z) - p(z)$ have the same norm, i.e. all $x \ne z$ with $p(x) = p(z)$ have the same
distance to $z$. Then there is a critical point $c$ of $p$ such that
$|p(z) - p(c)|/|z-c| \le (d-1)/d \cdot |p'(z)|$.
-/

@[category research solved, AMS 12]
lemma mean_value_problem_of_roots_same_norm (p : Polynomial ℂ) (hp : 2 ≤ p.natDegree) (z : ℂ)
    (h : ∀ x y : ℂ, p.eval x = p.eval z → p.eval y = p.eval z → x ≠ z → y ≠ z →
      ‖x - z‖ = ‖y - z‖) (K : ℝ) :
    ∃ c : ℂ, p.derivative.eval c = 0 ∧
      ‖p.eval z - p.eval c‖ / ‖z - c‖ ≤ (p.natDegree - 1)/ p.natDegree * ‖p.derivative.eval z‖ := by
  sorry

end MeanValueProblem

reformulations.difference: The literature commonly restricts the base point to p'(z) ≠ 0 and writes the modulus of a complex quotient. Lean quantifies over every z, uses the quotient of norms, and does not explicitly require c ≠ z.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For a noncritical z, the equation p'(c) = 0 forces c ≠ z, and norm_div identifies the two quotient expressions. If p'(z) = 0, the additional Lean instance is automatically satisfied by c = z: both sides are zero. Thus including critical base points adds only trivial instances and preserves the conjecture. The pointwise equivalence was proved for an arbitrary real bound in /workspace/review/equivalences.lean.

reformulations.difference: As with the main conjecture, Lean includes critical base points, whereas the precise source formulation usually assumes p'(z) ≠ 0.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: At a noncritical base point a critical witness is necessarily distinct from z, and the quotient of norms equals the norm of the quotient. At a critical base point c = z proves the added instance with bound 4. The same Lean-proved equivalence applies with A = 4.

reformulations.difference: The normalized real-root special case is expressed at an arbitrary base point using the fiber condition ∀ x, p(x) = p(z) → Im(x) = Im(z), rather than a root predicate on a polynomial fixing zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Set q(W) = p(W + z) - p(z). Its roots are exactly w = x - z with p(x) = p(z), and Im(w) = 0 exactly when Im(x) = Im(z). Also q(0) = 0, deg(q) = deg(p), and q'(w) = p'(w + z). Translating a critical witness by z preserves the inequality. Critical base points add only the trivial witness c = z. Both the root-condition equivalence and the universally quantified theorem's equivalence to the normalized, noncritical formulation were proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The normalized equal-modulus special case is expressed as equality of distances from z among the non-base points of the fiber p⁻¹(p(z)).
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For q(W) = p(W + z) - p(z), its nonzero roots are precisely x - z where p(x) = p(z) and x ≠ z. Consequently the pairwise distance hypothesis is exactly equality of the norms of q's nonzero roots. Translation preserves degree, critical points and the mean-value inequality. The possible critical-base-point cases are trivial, including cases with no nonzero normalized roots. The full equivalence with the normalized, noncritical formulation was proved in Lean.

review.notes:
All four declarations were checked. Lean experiments confirmed that the two degree hypotheses are equivalent, exclude zero/constant/linear polynomials, and that (p.natDegree - 1) / p.natDegree uses real subtraction and division; its degree-two value is 1/2. Both special-case hypotheses have noncritical quadratic instances, and the sharp quadratic inequality was verified independently. The unused real parameter K is mathematically harmless. The equivalence proofs compile without sorryAx dependencies.

The directly cited AMS and Elsevier full texts were inaccessible; accessible scholarly sources were used for cross-checking. Wikipedia currently has an unsupported 'disproved in 2026' short description and solved category, but its body still presents the conjecture without a disproof reference. Jatar–Ng, submitted 27 August 2026, explicitly says it is 'still unsolved.' This inconsistent Wikipedia metadata is not sufficient to establish a stale Lean status tag, so no confirmed status issue is reported.
